name: Aaron
who: Older brother of Moses, his spokesman before Pharaoh, and the first high priest of Israel.
key: God appointed Aaron to speak for Moses and sent him to meet his brother (Exodus 4).
Before Pharaoh, Aaron's staff became a serpent and swallowed the magicians' staffs (Exodus 7).

name: Abda
who: The father of Adoniram, the official who oversaw forced labor in Solomon's kingdom.
key: Abda is named as the father of Adoniram in the list of Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).
His son Adoniram was placed in charge of the forced labor for Solomon's building projects (1 Kings 4).

name: Abdon
who: A minor judge of Israel from Pirathon in Ephraim, son of Hillel, who judged Israel eight years.
key: After Elon, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel (Judges 12).
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys (Judges 12).

name: Abel
who: Second son of Adam and Eve, a shepherd whose offering God accepted, murdered by his brother Cain.
key: A keeper of sheep, he offered firstborn of his flock, and the LORD regarded his offering (Genesis 4).
His brother Cain killed him in the field (Genesis 4).

name: Abijah
who: Samuel's second son, who judged in Beersheba with his brother Joel but took bribes and perverted justice.
key: Samuel made his sons Joel and Abijah judges in Beersheba (1 Samuel 8).
They turned aside after gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8).

name: Abiathar
who: A priest, son of Ahimelech, who escaped Saul's massacre and served David.
key: Abiathar alone escaped when Saul killed the priests of Nob, and fled to David (1 Samuel 22).
He brought the ephod, through which David inquired of the Lord (1 Samuel 30).

name: Abida
who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: Abida is listed among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave his concubines' sons gifts and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Abidan
who: The son of Gideoni and chief of the tribe of Benjamin in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Benjamin to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Benjamin in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Abiel
who: A Benjaminite, the son of Zeror, and grandfather of King Saul through Kish.
key: He is named as the father of Kish, a wealthy Benjaminite and Saul's father (1 Samuel 9).
Kish, Saul's father, and Ner, Abner's father, are called sons of Abiel (1 Samuel 14).

name: Abiezer
who: A descendant of Manasseh through Gilead whose clan, the Abiezrites, produced the judge Gideon.
key: Iezer, ancestor of the clan of the Iezerites, is listed among the sons of Gilead (Numbers 26).
The clan of Abiezer received an allotment of land within the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17).

name: Abigail
who: Wise and discerning wife of Nabal who later became a wife of David.
key: She brought provisions to David and kept him from taking vengeance (1 Samuel 25).
After Nabal died, David sent for her and she became his wife (1 Samuel 25).

name: Abigail
who: A sister of David and Zeruiah, and the mother of Amasa, commander of Absalom's army.
key: She and Zeruiah are listed as sisters of David and his brothers (1 Chronicles 2).
She married Jether, also called Ithra, and bore him a son, Amasa (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Abihail
who: Wife of Abishur in Judah's line of Jerahmeel, and mother of Ahban and Molid.
key: Abishur's wife was named Abihail (1 Chronicles 2).
She bore him Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Abihail
who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Huri, whose seven sons headed Gadite families in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail son of Huri is traced back through Jaroah, Gilead, and Michael in Gad's genealogy (1 Chronicles 5).
His sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Abihail
who: A daughter of Eliab, David's eldest brother, named in the family line of King Rehoboam's wife Mahalath.
key: Abihail was the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse, making her David's niece (2 Chronicles 11).
She is named in the parentage of Mahalath, who married Rehoboam and bore him three sons (2 Chronicles 11).

name: Abihu
who: The second son of Aaron, ordained as a priest, who died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord.
key: He went up Mount Sinai with Moses and the elders and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24).
He was set apart with his brothers to serve the Lord as a priest (Exodus 28).

name: Abijah
who: A young son of King Jeroboam of Israel whose illness and death fulfilled the prophet Ahijah's word.
key: When Abijah fell sick, Jeroboam sent his wife in disguise to the prophet Ahijah at Shiloh (1 Kings 14).
Ahijah said the child would die, the only one of Jeroboam's house to be properly buried (1 Kings 14).

name: Abijah
who: A priest of David's time whose family formed the eighth priestly division, to which Zechariah later belonged.
key: When David organized the priests by lot, the eighth lot fell to Abijah (1 Chronicles 24).
Centuries later, Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, served as a priest of the division of Abijah (Luke 1).

name: Abijah
who: King of Judah, son of Rehoboam, who reigned three years in Jerusalem.
key: Rehoboam appointed him chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king (2 Chronicles 11).
He became king and walked in all the sins of his father (1 Kings 15).

name: Abimelech
who: A Philistine king of Gerar who dealt with Abraham and with Isaac.
key: Abimelech took Sarah, but God warned him in a dream and he returned her (Genesis 20).
Abraham prayed, and God healed Abimelech's household (Genesis 20).

name: Abimelech
who: A son of Gideon by a concubine in Shechem, who made himself king by murder.
key: Abimelech was born to Gideon's concubine in Shechem (Judges 8).
He killed his seventy brothers on one stone, and Shechem made him king (Judges 9).

name: Abinadab
who: A man of Kiriath-jearim who kept the ark of the covenant in his house for many years.
key: After the Philistines returned the ark, it was brought to Abinadab's house on the hill (1 Samuel 7).
His son Eleazar was consecrated to keep the ark, which stayed there twenty years (1 Samuel 7).

name: Abinadab
who: The second son of Jesse and an older brother of King David.
key: Jesse had Abinadab pass before Samuel, but the LORD had not chosen him (1 Samuel 16).
He was one of Jesse's three oldest sons who followed Saul to fight the Philistines (1 Samuel 17).

name: Abinadab
who: A son of King Saul who died with his father in battle against the Philistines.
key: He is listed among the sons of Saul (1 Chronicles 8).
The Philistines killed him with Jonathan and Malchi-shua on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31).

name: Abinoam
who: The father of Barak, the commander from Kedesh in Naphtali who fought Sisera alongside Deborah.
key: Deborah summoned his son Barak from Kedesh-naphtali to lead Israel against Sisera (Judges 4).
The Song of Deborah calls on Barak son of Abinoam to lead away his captives (Judges 5).

name: Abiram
who: Reubenite son of Eliab who, with his brother Dathan, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses.
key: With Dathan and Korah, he rose up against the leadership of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
He and Dathan refused Moses' summons, accusing him of failing to bring them to the promised land (Numbers 16).

name: Abiram
who: Firstborn son of Hiel of Bethel, who died when his father laid the foundation of rebuilt Jericho.
key: Joshua had declared that whoever rebuilt Jericho would lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn (Joshua 6).
When Hiel laid Jericho's foundation in Ahab's day, it cost him his firstborn Abiram (1 Kings 16).

name: Abishag
who: A young woman from Shunem who attended King David in his old age.
key: She was chosen to care for the aged David and keep him warm (1 Kings 1).
She was attending the king when Bathsheba came to speak about Adonijah (1 Kings 1).

name: Abishai
who: A son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one of David's chief warriors.
key: Abishai went with David into Saul's camp and offered to kill Saul (1 Samuel 26).
With Joab he killed Abner to avenge their brother Asahel (2 Samuel 3).

name: Abishua
who: A priest descended from Aaron, son of Phinehas and father of Bukki, in the high-priestly line.
key: Phinehas son of Eleazar fathered Abishua, and Abishua fathered Bukki (1 Chronicles 6).
He is named again among Aaron's descendants through Eleazar (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Abishur
who: A man of Judah in Jerahmeel's line, son of Shammai, husband of Abihail, and father of Ahban and Molid.
key: Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur (1 Chronicles 2).
Abishur's wife Abihail bore him Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Abner
who: Son of Ner, Saul's relative and the commander of Saul's army.
key: He was commander of King Saul's army (1 Samuel 14).
After David killed Goliath, Abner brought him to Saul (1 Samuel 17).

name: Abraham
who: Patriarch called by God to go to Canaan, with whom God made a covenant to bless all nations.
key: God called Abram to leave his country and promised to make him a great nation (Genesis 12).
He believed the Lord, and God counted it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15).

name: Absalom
who: Son of David by Maacah who rebelled against his father and tried to seize the throne.
key: He killed his half-brother Amnon for violating his sister Tamar, then fled (2 Samuel 13).
Joab arranged his return to Jerusalem and reconciliation with David (2 Samuel 14).

name: Achaicus
who: A believer from Corinth who, with Stephanas and Fortunatus, visited Paul and refreshed his spirit.
key: Paul rejoiced at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus from the Corinthian church (1 Corinthians 16).
They made up for the Corinthians' absence and refreshed Paul's spirit (1 Corinthians 16).

name: Achan
who: A man of Judah, son of Carmi, who took devoted things from Jericho and brought trouble on Israel.
key: He secretly took a cloak, silver, and gold devoted to the Lord from Jericho (Joshua 7).
Because of his sin, Israel was defeated at Ai (Joshua 7).

name: Achish
who: Philistine king of Gath who sheltered David while David was fleeing from Saul.
key: David pretended to be insane before him in order to escape (1 Samuel 21).
He later received David and his men and gave him the town of Ziklag (1 Samuel 27).

name: Achsah
who: The daughter of Caleb, given in marriage to Othniel after he captured Kiriath-sepher (Debir).
key: Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to the man who captured Kiriath-sepher (Joshua 15).
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured the city and married Achsah (Joshua 15).

name: Adah
who: A Hittite wife of Esau, daughter of Elon, and mother of Eliphaz.
key: Esau's marriage to a daughter of Elon the Hittite grieved Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26).
She is named as Esau's wife, the daughter of Elon the Hittite (Genesis 36).

name: Adah
who: One of the two wives of Lamech, a descendant of Cain, and mother of Jabal and Jubal.
key: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
Adah bore Jabal, father of those who live in tents and keep livestock (Genesis 4).

name: Adaiah
who: A priest descended from Pashhur, son of Jeroham, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile.
key: Adaiah son of Jeroham is listed among the priests who settled in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah's list of Jerusalem's residents also names him among the priests serving there (Nehemiah 11).

name: Adam
who: The first man, formed by God from dust and placed in the garden of Eden.
key: God formed Adam from the dust and placed him in Eden (Genesis 2).
God made the woman from Adam's rib and brought her to him (Genesis 2).

name: Adoni-bezek
who: A Canaanite king at Bezek defeated by Judah and Simeon after Joshua's death.
key: The men of Judah and Simeon defeated Adoni-bezek's forces at Bezek and captured him (Judges 1).
They cut off his thumbs and big toes, as he had done to seventy kings (Judges 1).

name: Adoni-zedek
who: The Amorite king of Jerusalem who led a coalition of five kings against Gibeon and Joshua.
key: Alarmed that Gibeon had made peace with Israel, he called four Amorite kings to attack Gibeon (Joshua 10).
Joshua defeated the coalition, and the LORD threw down great hailstones on the fleeing armies (Joshua 10).

name: Adonijah
who: David's fourth son, born to Haggith, who tried to take the throne before Solomon.
key: Adonijah was born to David by Haggith at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
In David's old age, he declared himself king with Joab and Abiathar's support (1 Kings 1).

name: Adoniram
who: The son of Abda who oversaw forced labor under David, Solomon, and Rehoboam.
key: He was in charge of the forced labor under David (2 Samuel 20).
He is listed among Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).

name: Aeneas
who: A paralyzed man at Lydda, bedridden for eight years, whom Peter healed in the name of Jesus.
key: Peter found Aeneas at Lydda, paralyzed and bedridden for eight years (Acts 9).
Peter told him Jesus Christ healed him, and Aeneas rose immediately (Acts 9).

name: Agabus
who: A Christian prophet from Judea who foretold a great famine and Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.
key: Agabus came to Antioch and predicted by the Spirit a great famine over the world (Acts 11).
The famine came under Claudius, and the disciples sent relief to the believers in Judea (Acts 11).

name: Agag
who: A king of the Amalekites whom Saul spared against the Lord's command.
key: Saul captured Agag alive and spared him along with the best livestock (1 Samuel 15).
Samuel rebuked Saul, saying the Lord had rejected him as king (1 Samuel 15).

name: Agee
who: A Hararite, the father of Shammah, one of David's three chief mighty men.
key: Agee the Hararite is named as the father of Shammah among David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
His son Shammah held a field of lentils and struck down the Philistines (2 Samuel 23).

name: Agrippa
who: King Agrippa II, a ruler of the Herod family who heard the apostle Paul's defense at Caesarea.
key: He and Bernice visited Festus, who told them about Paul's case (Acts 25).
Festus brought Paul before Agrippa to help frame charges for the emperor (Acts 25).

name: Agur
who: The son of Jakeh and author of the wise sayings collected in Proverbs 30.
key: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh open with his confession of limited understanding (Proverbs 30).
He affirms that every word of God proves true and must not be added to (Proverbs 30).

name: Ahab
who: Son of Omri and king of Israel who, with his wife Jezebel, promoted Baal worship and opposed Elijah.
key: He married Jezebel and built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria (1 Kings 16).
Elijah defeated the prophets of Baal before him on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).

name: Ahab
who: A false prophet among the exiles in Babylon, son of Kolaiah, whom Jeremiah condemned for prophesying lies.
key: Jeremiah declared that Ahab and Zedekiah were prophesying lies to the exiles in the LORD's name (Jeremiah 29).
The LORD said Nebuchadnezzar would kill them, and their fate would become a curse among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).

name: Ahasbai
who: A man of Maacah whose son Eliphelet was one of David's mighty men.
key: Ahasbai is named as the father of Eliphelet in the list of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
His son Eliphelet belonged to David's elite warriors known as the thirty (2 Samuel 23).

name: Ahasuerus
who: The king of Persia who made Esther his queen.
key: Ahasuerus ruled 127 provinces and deposed Queen Vashti for refusing his summons (Esther 1).
He chose Esther as queen in Vashti's place (Esther 2).

name: Ahaz
who: A king of Judah, son of Jotham, who turned to idols and to Assyria.
key: Ahaz did not do right and even burned his son as an offering (2 Kings 16).
When Syria and Israel attacked, Isaiah urged him to trust God and gave the Immanuel sign (Isaiah 7).

name: Ahaz
who: A descendant of King Saul through Jonathan and Mephibosheth, listed in the genealogy of Benjamin.
key: Ahaz was a son of Micah, the son of Merib-baal, Jonathan's son (1 Chronicles 8).
He fathered Jehoaddah, continuing Saul's family line through later generations (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Ahaziah
who: A son of Ahab who reigned two years as king of Israel and served Baal.
key: He became king in Samaria, did evil, and served Baal as his parents had (1 Kings 22).
Jehoshaphat joined him in building ships at Ezion-geber, but the ships were wrecked (2 Chronicles 20).

name: Ahaziah
who: A king of Judah, son of Jehoram and Athaliah, who reigned one year.
key: Ahaziah became king at twenty-two and followed the ways of Ahab's house (2 Kings 8).
He joined Joram of Israel in war against Hazael at Ramoth-gilead (2 Kings 8).

name: Ahban
who: A man of Judah in Jerahmeel's line, son of Abishur and his wife Abihail.
key: Abishur's wife Abihail bore him Ahban and Molid (1 Chronicles 2).
He is listed among the descendants of Jerahmeel, son of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ahiezer
who: The son of Ammishaddai and chief of the tribe of Dan in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Dan to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Dan in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Ahijah
who: A prophet from Shiloh who foretold Jeroboam's rule over ten tribes and later the downfall of his house.
key: He tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam (1 Kings 11).
The division of the kingdom fulfilled the word the Lord spoke through Ahijah (1 Kings 12).

name: Ahijah
who: A man of the tribe of Issachar, father of Baasha, who seized the throne of Israel.
key: His son Baasha of Issachar killed King Nadab and struck down Jeroboam's whole house (1 Kings 15).
Baasha son of Ahijah reigned over Israel twenty-four years in Tirzah (1 Kings 15).

name: Ahijah
who: A son of Jerahmeel in the tribe of Judah, listed in the genealogy of Hezron's descendants.
key: Ahijah is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).
Through Hezron and Perez, his family belonged to the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Ahikam
who: Royal official under King Josiah, son of Shaphan, who protected the prophet Jeremiah.
key: Josiah sent him with others to inquire of the prophetess Huldah about the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22).
He protected Jeremiah so that he was not handed over to be put to death (Jeremiah 26).

name: Ahilud
who: The father of Jehoshaphat, David's recorder, and of Baana, one of Solomon's officers.
key: His son Jehoshaphat served as recorder in David's court (2 Samuel 8).
Jehoshaphat is again listed as recorder among David's officials (2 Samuel 20).

name: Ahimaaz
who: A son of Zadok the priest who served as a swift messenger for David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: He and Jonathan, son of Abiathar, were stationed to carry news from Jerusalem to David (2 Samuel 15).
Hiding in a well at Bahurim, he escaped Absalom's men and warned David to cross the Jordan (2 Samuel 17).

name: Ahiman
who: One of the three sons of Anak, the giant Anakim living at Hebron when Israel entered Canaan.
key: Israel's spies found Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, living at Hebron (Numbers 13).
Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak from Hebron (Joshua 15).

name: Ahimelech
who: The priest at Nob, son of Ahitub, who helped David and was killed by Saul's order.
key: He gave the fleeing David holy bread and the sword of Goliath (1 Samuel 21).
Saul accused him of conspiracy, and Doeg the Edomite killed him and the priests of Nob (1 Samuel 22).

name: Ahimelech
who: A son of Abiathar who served as a priest alongside Zadok during David's reign.
key: He and Zadok are listed as priests in David's administration (2 Samuel 8).
Chronicles repeats his place as priest among David's officials (1 Chronicles 18).

name: Ahinoam
who: A woman of Jezreel who became David's wife and the mother of his firstborn son, Amnon.
key: David married Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Samuel 25).
She lived with David among the Philistines at Gath (1 Samuel 27).

name: Ahio
who: A son of Abinadab who helped drive the cart carrying the ark when David first tried to move it.
key: Ahio walked before the ark while he and Uzzah drove the new cart from Abinadab's house (2 Samuel 6).
When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah took hold of the ark, and God struck him down (2 Samuel 6).

name: Ahira
who: The son of Enan and chief of the tribe of Naphtali in the wilderness.
key: Named chief of the tribe of Naphtali to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
Led the army of Naphtali in its assigned place around the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Ahisamach
who: A man of the tribe of Dan, father of the craftsman Oholiab, who helped build the tabernacle.
key: The LORD appointed his son Oholiab of Dan to work with Bezalel on the tabernacle (Exodus 31).
Moses announced that God had given Oholiab son of Ahisamach the ability to teach others (Exodus 35).

name: Ahishahar
who: A Benjaminite, son of Bilhan, whose family was counted among Benjamin's mighty warriors.
key: The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
They were heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200 able to go to war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Ahithophel
who: David's trusted counselor from Giloh who joined Absalom's rebellion.
key: He joined Absalom's conspiracy, and David prayed his counsel would become foolishness (2 Samuel 15).
He advised Absalom to go in to his father's concubines publicly (2 Samuel 16).

name: Ahitub
who: A priest, grandson of Eli through Phinehas, and father of Ahijah and Ahimelech.
key: His son Ahijah served as priest, wearing the ephod, with Saul's army (1 Samuel 14).
Saul summoned his son Ahimelech and the priests of his house, and Doeg killed them (1 Samuel 22).

name: Ahitub
who: A priest descended from Aaron, the son of Amariah and father of Zadok.
key: His son Zadok served as priest under David (2 Samuel 8).
He is listed in the priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Oholiab
who: A craftsman from the tribe of Dan who assisted Bezalel in building the tabernacle.
key: The Lord appointed him, son of Ahisamach, to work with Bezalel (Exodus 31).
God gave him and Bezalel skill and the ability to teach others (Exodus 35).

name: Oholibamah
who: One of Esau's wives, a Canaanite woman descended from Zibeon the Hivite.
key: Esau took her as a wife from the Canaanite women (Genesis 36).
She bore Esau three sons, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah, in Canaan (Genesis 36).

name: Aiah
who: The father of Rizpah, the concubine of King Saul.
key: His daughter Rizpah was a concubine of King Saul (2 Samuel 3).
Ish-bosheth accused Abner of going in to Rizpah daughter of Aiah (2 Samuel 3).

name: Aiah
who: A Horite, son of Zibeon and brother of Anah, among the clans of Seir in Edom.
key: The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah, the Anah who found the hot springs (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats the sons of Zibeon as Aiah and Anah (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Akan
who: A Horite, son of the chief Ezer, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Akan is listed among the sons of Ezer, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the Horite genealogy of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Akkub
who: A Levite gatekeeper whose name also marks a family of gatekeepers after the exile.
key: He is listed among the gatekeepers who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 9).
The sons of Akkub were among the gatekeepers who returned from exile (Ezra 2).

name: Akkub
who: Ancestor of a family of temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.
key: The sons of Akkub are listed among the temple servants who returned from exile (Ezra 2).
The temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants numbered 392 in all (Ezra 2).

name: Alemeth
who: A Benjaminite descendant of King Saul through Jonathan, son of Jarah, also called Jehoaddah.
key: Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, in the line of Saul through Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy repeated before Saul's death calls their father Jarah (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Alexander
who: A son of Simon of Cyrene, the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross.
key: Mark identifies Simon of Cyrene as the father of Alexander and Rufus (Mark 15).
His father, coming in from the country, was compelled by soldiers to carry Jesus' cross (Mark 15).

name: Alexander
who: A member of the high-priestly family who sat with the council that questioned Peter and John.
key: The day after Peter and John's arrest, rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem (Acts 4).
Alexander was there with Annas, Caiaphas, and John, all of the high-priestly family (Acts 4).

name: Alexander
who: A man who rejected faith and a good conscience, whom Paul handed over to Satan.
key: Paul named Hymenaeus and Alexander as men who had made shipwreck of their faith (1 Timothy 1).
Paul handed them over to Satan so they would learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1).

name: Alphaeus
who: The father of James, one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
key: Jesus named James son of Alphaeus among the twelve apostles he sent out (Matthew 10).
Mark's list of the twelve also includes James son of Alphaeus (Mark 3).

name: Alvan
who: A Horite, son of Shobal, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Alvan is listed first among the sons of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the genealogy of Seir's descendants (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Amalek
who: A grandson of Esau, son of Eliphaz by Timna, and ancestor of the Amalekites.
key: Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz, Esau's son (Genesis 36).
He is listed among the chiefs descended from Esau in Edom (Genesis 36).

name: Amariah
who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Meraioth and grandfather of Zadok, high priest under David.
key: Amariah son of Meraioth is listed in the priestly line from Aaron to the exile (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Ahitub was the father of Zadok, who served as priest under David (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Amariah
who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Azariah and father of Ahitub, named among Ezra's ancestors.
key: Amariah son of Azariah is listed in the high priestly line descended from Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).
Ezra's genealogy traces his ancestry back to Aaron through Amariah (Ezra 7).

name: Amariah
who: A Levite of Kohath's line, second son of Hebron, listed in David's organization of the Levites.
key: Amariah is named as the second son of Hebron among the Levites David organized (1 Chronicles 23).
He appears again among the Levite family heads who cast lots like the priests (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Amariah
who: The chief priest under King Jehoshaphat, placed over all matters concerning the LORD.
key: Jehoshaphat appointed judges in Jerusalem and charged them to serve in the fear of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19).
He set Amariah the chief priest over every matter of the LORD (2 Chronicles 19).

name: Amariah
who: An ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah, son of Hezekiah and father of Gedaliah.
key: Zephaniah was son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah (Zephaniah 1).
The word of the LORD came to his descendant Zephaniah in the days of Josiah king of Judah (Zephaniah 1).

name: Amasa
who: A nephew of David, son of Abigail, who commanded Absalom's army and later David's, until Joab killed him.
key: Absalom appointed him commander of the army in place of Joab (2 Samuel 17).
After the revolt David promised to make him commander instead of Joab (2 Samuel 19).

name: Amasai
who: Chief of the thirty, who pledged loyalty to David when men of Benjamin and Judah joined him.
key: Men of Benjamin and Judah came to David's stronghold, and David questioned their intentions (1 Chronicles 12).
The Spirit clothed Amasai, and he declared loyalty and peace to David and his helpers (1 Chronicles 12).

name: Amaziah
who: A king of Judah, son of Joash, who began well but turned to Edom's gods.
key: He executed his father's murderers but spared their children, as the Law commanded (2 Kings 14).
At a prophet's word, he sent home the Israelite soldiers he had hired (2 Chronicles 25).

name: Amaziah
who: The priest of Bethel who opposed the prophet Amos during the reign of Jeroboam II.
key: Amaziah reported to Jeroboam that Amos was conspiring against him in Israel (Amos 7).
He told Amos to flee to Judah and stop prophesying at Bethel, the king's sanctuary (Amos 7).

name: Amittai
who: The father of the prophet Jonah, from Gath-hepher in Israel.
key: His son Jonah of Gath-hepher prophesied that Jeroboam II would restore Israel's borders (2 Kings 14).
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai to go to Nineveh (Jonah 1).

name: Ammiel
who: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, who sheltered Mephibosheth and later supplied David.
key: Mephibosheth was living in the house of Machir son of Ammiel at Lo-debar (2 Samuel 9).
Machir son of Ammiel brought supplies to David at Mahanaim while he fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 17).

name: Ammihud
who: An Ephraimite, father of Elishama the tribal leader, and an ancestor of Joshua.
key: His son Elishama was appointed leader of Ephraim for the census (Numbers 1).
Elishama son of Ammihud led Ephraim's camp on the west side (Numbers 2).

name: Ammihud
who: Father of Talmai, the king of Geshur with whom Absalom took refuge.
key: After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur (2 Samuel 13).
Absalom stayed in Geshur with Ammihud's son for three years (2 Samuel 13).

name: Amminadab
who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, father of Nahshon, and an ancestor of King David and of Jesus.
key: His daughter Elisheba married Aaron (Exodus 6).
His son Nahshon was appointed chief of the tribe of Judah (Numbers 1).

name: Ammishaddai
who: A man of the tribe of Dan, the father of Ahiezer, Dan's chief in the wilderness.
key: He is named as the father of Ahiezer, chief of Dan, at the census (Numbers 1).
His son Ahiezer led Dan's army north of the tabernacle (Numbers 2).

name: Amnon
who: David's firstborn son, by Ahinoam, who was killed by Absalom.
key: Amnon was born to David by Ahinoam at Hebron (2 Samuel 3).
He violated his half-sister Tamar and then hated her (2 Samuel 13).

name: Amon
who: King of Judah, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, who did evil and was assassinated.
key: He became king at twenty-two and reigned two years, doing evil like Manasseh (2 Kings 21).
He did not humble himself before the LORD as his father had (2 Chronicles 33).

name: Amorites
label: People group
who: A people descended from Canaan who held much of the land, west and east of the Jordan, before Israel's conquest.
key: The Amorites are listed among the descendants of Canaan son of Ham (Genesis 10).
God told Abram the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet complete (Genesis 15).

name: Amos
who: A shepherd from Tekoa whom the Lord called to prophesy against Israel and the nations.
key: He prophesied in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam, two years before the earthquake (Amos 1).
He saw visions of locusts, fire, and a plumb line, and interceded for Israel (Amos 7).

name: Amoz
who: The father of the prophet Isaiah, named whenever Scripture identifies Isaiah as the son of Amoz.
key: Isaiah's vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem is introduced as the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz (Isaiah 1).
Isaiah son of Amoz sent King Hezekiah God's answer concerning Sennacherib of Assyria (2 Kings 19).

name: Amram
who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, husband of Jochebed, and father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
key: He married his father's sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses; he lived 137 years (Exodus 6).
His descendants formed the clan of the Amramites among the Kohathites (Numbers 3).

name: Amzi
who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, listed in the ancestry of Ethan, a singer appointed in David's time.
key: Amzi appears in the genealogy of Ethan, the Merarite singer who stood at Heman's left (1 Chronicles 6).
He is named as the son of Bani and the father of Hilkiah (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Anah
who: The parent of Esau's wife Oholibamah, described as the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite.
key: Esau married Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite (Genesis 36).
Her daughter Oholibamah bore Esau three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah (Genesis 36).

name: Anah
who: A son of Seir the Horite and one of the Horite chiefs in Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Seir, the original inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
He is named among the chiefs of the Horites in Seir (Genesis 36).

name: Anah
who: A Horite, son of Zibeon, remembered for finding hot springs in the wilderness.
key: Anah and Aiah are listed as the sons of Zibeon in the line of Seir (Genesis 36).
He found the hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father's donkeys (Genesis 36).

name: Anak
who: Son of Arba and ancestor of the Anakim, the tall people of Hebron who frightened Israel's spies.
key: The spies saw descendants of Anak at Hebron and felt like grasshoppers beside them (Numbers 13).
Moses assured Israel that God would defeat the sons of Anak before them (Deuteronomy 9).

name: Anani
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the seven sons of Elioenai.
key: The sons of Elioenai were Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belonged to the royal line of Zerubbabel and King Jehoiachin (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Ananias
who: A member of the Jerusalem church who died after lying to the Holy Spirit about a gift.
key: With his wife Sapphira's knowledge, Ananias sold property and kept back part of the money (Acts 5).
He brought the rest to the apostles as if it were the full amount (Acts 5).

name: Ananias
who: A disciple in Damascus whom the Lord sent to restore Saul's sight.
key: In a vision, the Lord sent him to Saul, though he feared Saul's reputation (Acts 9).
He laid hands on Saul, who regained his sight and was baptized (Acts 9).

name: Ananias
who: The high priest who ordered Paul struck before the council and later accused him before Governor Felix.
key: When Paul spoke before the council, Ananias commanded those near him to strike Paul on the mouth (Acts 23).
Paul answered that God would strike him, calling him a whitewashed wall (Acts 23).

name: Anath
who: The father of Shamgar, the deliverer who struck down six hundred Philistines.
key: Shamgar son of Anath killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad and saved Israel (Judges 3).
Deborah's song recalls that in the days of Shamgar son of Anath the highways were abandoned (Judges 5).

name: Andrew
who: A fisherman from Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter, and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
key: A disciple of John the Baptist, he followed Jesus and brought his brother Simon to him (John 1).
Jesus called him and Peter from their nets to become fishers of men (Matthew 4).

name: Aner
who: An Amorite near Hebron, brother of Mamre and Eshcol, who was allied with Abram.
key: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre the Amorite were allies of Abram, who lived by the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 14).
They went with Abram when he pursued the kings who had captured Lot (Genesis 14).

name: Anna
who: An elderly prophetess of the tribe of Asher who recognized the infant Jesus in the temple.
key: Widowed after seven years of marriage, Anna worshiped in the temple with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2).
When Jesus was presented at the temple, she came up and gave thanks to God (Luke 2).

name: Annas
who: An influential Jewish high priest, father-in-law of Caiaphas, who questioned Jesus first after his arrest.
key: God's word came to John the Baptist during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas (Luke 3).
After his arrest, Jesus was taken first to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas (John 18).

name: Antipas
who: A faithful witness of Christ who was put to death in Pergamum, where Satan dwells.
key: The risen Christ called Antipas my faithful witness (Revelation 2).
He was killed among the believers in Pergamum, where Satan's throne is (Revelation 2).

name: Apollos
who: A Jewish believer from Alexandria, eloquent in the Scriptures, who ministered in Ephesus and Corinth.
key: Priscilla and Aquila explained the way of God more accurately to him in Ephesus (Acts 18).
In Achaia he powerfully refuted the Jews, showing from Scripture that Jesus was the Christ (Acts 18).

name: Aquila
who: A Jewish believer from Pontus, a tentmaker who with his wife Priscilla worked alongside Paul.
key: Expelled from Rome under Claudius, he and Priscilla worked with Paul as tentmakers in Corinth (Acts 18).
In Ephesus they explained the way of God more accurately to Apollos (Acts 18).

name: Arad
who: A Benjaminite, son of Beriah, listed among the family heads in Benjamin's genealogy.
key: Arad is listed among the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8).
His father Beriah was a family head of Aijalon who drove out the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Aran
who: A Horite, son of Dishan, among the early inhabitants of Seir.
key: Aran and Uz are listed as the sons of Dishan, a Horite descendant of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name in the genealogy of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Arba
who: The greatest man among the Anakim and father of Anak, after whom Kiriath-arba (Hebron) was named.
key: Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakim (Joshua 14).
Caleb received Kiriath-arba as his portion; Arba was the father of Anak (Joshua 15).

name: Archelaus
who: A son of Herod the Great who ruled Judea after his father's death.
key: After Herod died, Archelaus reigned over Judea in place of his father (Matthew 2).
Joseph was afraid to settle there and, warned in a dream, withdrew to Nazareth in Galilee (Matthew 2).

name: Aristarchus
who: A Macedonian from Thessalonica who traveled with Paul and shared his imprisonment.
key: The rioting crowd in Ephesus seized him and Gaius, Paul's companions (Acts 19).
He accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece toward Jerusalem (Acts 20).

name: Armoni
who: A son of King Saul by his concubine Rizpah, handed over to the Gibeonites and put to death.
key: Armoni and his brother Mephibosheth were sons whom Rizpah bore to Saul (2 Samuel 21).
David gave them and five of Saul's grandsons to the Gibeonites, who hanged them (2 Samuel 21).

name: Arpachshad
who: A son of Shem born two years after the flood, and an ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shem in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Born two years after the flood, he fathered Shelah at thirty-five (Genesis 11).

name: Artaxerxes
who: The Persian king who, after receiving a letter against Jerusalem, ordered the Jews to stop rebuilding the city.
key: Rehum, Shimshai, and their associates wrote to Artaxerxes, accusing Jerusalem of being rebellious (Ezra 4).
Artaxerxes had the records searched and found the city had a history of revolt (Ezra 4).

name: Artaxerxes
who: A king of Persia who authorized Ezra's mission and sent his cupbearer Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem.
key: The temple was finished according to decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes (Ezra 6).
He issued a letter granting Ezra authority, funds, and supplies for the temple (Ezra 7).

name: Artemas
who: A coworker of Paul whom he considered sending to Titus in Crete.
key: Paul planned to send Artemas or Tychicus to Titus (Titus 3).
Once one arrived, Titus was to come quickly to Paul at Nicopolis for the winter (Titus 3).

name: Asa
who: King of Judah, son of Abijah, who removed idols and relied on the Lord for much of his reign.
key: He removed idols and deposed his grandmother Maacah as queen mother (1 Kings 15).
He relied on the Lord and defeated Zerah the Ethiopian's huge army (2 Chronicles 14).

name: Asahel
who: Swift-footed nephew of David and brother of Joab, killed by Abner in battle.
key: Fast as a wild gazelle, he chased Abner after the battle at Gibeon (2 Samuel 2).
Abner warned him repeatedly, then killed him with the butt of his spear (2 Samuel 2).

name: Asaph
who: The father of Joah, the recorder who served King Hezekiah during the Assyrian threat.
key: His son Joah the recorder went with Eliakim and Shebna to meet the Assyrian Rabshakeh (2 Kings 18).
Joah son of Asaph returned with torn clothes and reported the Rabshakeh's words to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18).

name: Asaph
who: A Levite musician and seer appointed by David to lead worship before the ark.
key: David's Levites appointed Asaph to sound bronze cymbals in worship (1 Chronicles 15).
David put Asaph in charge of thanksgiving before the ark (1 Chronicles 16).

name: Asenath
who: An Egyptian woman, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, who became Joseph's wife.
key: Pharaoh gave Joseph Asenath, daughter of Potiphera priest of On, as his wife (Genesis 41).
Before the famine she bore Joseph two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41).

name: Asher
who: A son of Jacob by Zilpah, Leah's servant, and ancestor of the tribe of Asher.
key: Asher was born to Zilpah, and Leah named him, saying she was happy (Genesis 30).
He went down to Egypt with his sons and daughter Serah (Genesis 46).

name: Ashkenaz
who: A son of Gomer and great-grandson of Noah through Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations.
key: He is listed among the sons of Gomer, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats his name in the line of Japheth (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Ashvath
who: A man of the tribe of Asher, a son of Japhlet, named in Asher's genealogy.
key: Ashvath is listed as a son of Japhlet among the descendants of Asher (1 Chronicles 7).
His brothers were Pasach and Bimhal (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Asiel
who: A man of the tribe of Simeon, father of Seraiah and ancestor of the clan chief Jehu.
key: Asiel is named in Simeon's genealogy as the father of Seraiah and forefather of Jehu (1 Chronicles 4).
His descendants were among the Simeonite princes whose clans increased greatly (1 Chronicles 4).

name: Asshur
who: A son of Shem whose name is linked with the people of Assyria.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shem in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
He appears again among Shem's sons (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Asshurim
label: People group
who: An Arabian people descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham and Keturah.
key: The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim (Genesis 25).
Abraham gave gifts to his sons by his concubines and sent them east, away from Isaac (Genesis 25).

name: Atarah
who: A wife of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah and the mother of Onam.
key: She is named as another wife of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn son (1 Chronicles 2).
She bore Onam, whose descendants are traced in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Athaliah
who: Daughter of Ahab who seized the throne of Judah and ruled six years.
key: She was the wife of King Jehoram of Judah (2 Kings 8).
She counseled her son King Ahaziah to act wickedly (2 Chronicles 22).

name: Azaniah
who: A Levite whose son Jeshua sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day.
key: He is named as the father of the Levite Jeshua (Nehemiah 10).
His son Jeshua was among the Levites who set their seal on the covenant to keep God's law (Nehemiah 10).

name: Azariah
who: A Kohathite Levite listed among the ancestors of Heman, David's temple singer.
key: He appears in Heman's ancestry as son of Zephaniah and father of Joel (1 Chronicles 6).
The parallel list of Kohath's descendants appears to call him Uzziah son of Uriel (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Azariah
who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Ahimaaz and grandson of Zadok, in the days of Solomon.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Ahimaaz and father of Johanan (1 Chronicles 6).
He is possibly the Azariah son of Zadok named first among Solomon's high officials (1 Kings 4).

name: Azariah
who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of Johanan, noted as serving in Solomon's temple.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Johanan and father of Amariah (1 Chronicles 6).
Chronicles notes he served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Azariah
who: A priest in Aaron's line, son of the high priest Hilkiah and grandfather of Jehozadak.
key: He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Hilkiah and father of Seraiah (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Seraiah's son Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD sent Judah away (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Azariah
who: A prophet, son of Oded, who encouraged King Asa of Judah to seek the LORD.
key: The Spirit of God came on him, and he went out to meet Asa after a victory (2 Chronicles 15).
He told Asa the LORD is with them while they are with him (2 Chronicles 15).

name: Azariah
who: The chief priest who confronted King Uzziah when the king entered the temple to burn incense.
key: With eighty priests he withstood Uzziah, saying burning incense belonged to the consecrated priests (2 Chronicles 26).
Leprosy broke out on Uzziah's forehead, and Azariah and the priests rushed him out (2 Chronicles 26).

name: Azariah
who: A young man of Judah taken to Babylon with Daniel and renamed Abednego.
key: Taken to Babylon, he was chosen for royal training and renamed Abednego (Daniel 1).
He joined Daniel in refusing the king's food and proved healthier after ten days (Daniel 1).

name: Azbuk
who: The father of Nehemiah, the ruler of half of Beth-zur who helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
key: His son Nehemiah ruled half the district of Beth-zur (Nehemiah 3).
Nehemiah son of Azbuk repaired the wall as far as the tombs of David (Nehemiah 3).

name: Azmaveth
who: A Benjaminite descendant of King Saul through Jonathan, son of Jarah, also called Jehoaddah.
key: Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, in the line of Saul through Jonathan (1 Chronicles 8).
The genealogy repeated before Saul's death calls their father Jarah (1 Chronicles 9).

name: Azriel
who: The father of Seraiah, an officer King Jehoiakim sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch.
key: Azriel is known only as the father of Seraiah, one of King Jehoiakim's officers (Jeremiah 36).
After burning Jeremiah's scroll, Jehoiakim ordered Seraiah son of Azriel and others to seize Baruch and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 36).

name: Azrikam
who: A descendant of David in the royal line after the exile, a son of Neariah.
key: Azrikam is listed with Elioenai and Hizkiah as the sons of Neariah (1 Chronicles 3).
His family belongs to David's royal line traced on through Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Azubah
who: A wife of Caleb son of Hezron in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Caleb fathered children by his wife Azubah (1 Chronicles 2).
After Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Baal-zebub
label: False god
who: The god of the Philistine city of Ekron, consulted by King Ahaziah of Israel.
key: After falling through a lattice, Ahaziah sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover (2 Kings 1).
The LORD's angel sent Elijah to ask if there was no God in Israel (2 Kings 1).

name: Baal
label: False god
who: A Canaanite false god whose worship repeatedly led Israel into idolatry.
key: At Shittim Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD's anger brought a plague (Numbers 25).
Gideon tore down his father's altar to Baal and was called Jerubbaal (Judges 6).

name: Baal
who: A man of the tribe of Reuben listed in the genealogy of Joel's descendants.
key: He is listed in Reuben's line as son of Reaiah and father of Beerah (1 Chronicles 5).
His son Beerah, a Reubenite chief, was carried into exile by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Baana
who: Son of Ahilud and one of Solomon's twelve district officers who provided food for the king.
key: He governed Solomon's district of Taanach, Megiddo, and Beth-shean, as far as Abel-meholah (1 Kings 4).
Like the other officers, he supplied provisions for the king's household one month each year (1 Kings 4).

name: Baanah
who: A Benjaminite raiding captain who, with his brother Rechab, murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.
key: He and Rechab, sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, led raiding bands for Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4).
They entered Ish-bosheth's house at midday, killed him on his bed, and took his head (2 Samuel 4).

name: Baanah
who: A man of Netophah whose son Heleb was one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles names the son Heled son of Baanah of Netophah among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Baasha
who: A king of Israel from Issachar who seized the throne and destroyed Jeroboam's house.
key: Baasha killed King Nadab and struck down Jeroboam's whole house (1 Kings 15).
He fortified Ramah to cut off traffic to Asa king of Judah (1 Kings 15).

name: Balaam
who: Son of Beor, a diviner hired by King Balak of Moab to curse Israel.
key: Balak summoned him to curse Israel, and his donkey spoke to stop him (Numbers 22).
Instead of cursing Israel, he blessed them three times (Numbers 23–24).

name: Baladan
who: The father of Merodach-baladan, the king of Babylon who sent envoys to King Hezekiah.
key: Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a present to Hezekiah after his illness (2 Kings 20).
Isaiah's account likewise names the Babylonian king as the son of Baladan (Isaiah 39).

name: Balak
who: King of Moab, son of Zippor, who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
key: Fearing Israel, Balak sent for the prophet Balaam to curse them (Numbers 22).
Balaam blessed Israel instead each time Balak brought him to a new place (Numbers 23).

name: Bani
who: A Levite of Merari's clan, son of Shemer, in the ancestry of Ethan, a singer appointed by David.
key: Ethan's ancestry runs through Amzi son of Bani, son of Shemer (1 Chronicles 6).
Ethan and his Merarite brothers stood at Heman's left hand in the service of song (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Barabbas
who: A notorious prisoner whom Pilate released at the crowd's demand instead of Jesus.
key: Pilate offered to release Jesus or Barabbas, and the crowd chose Barabbas (Matthew 27).
He had been imprisoned with rebels who had committed murder in an insurrection (Mark 15).

name: Barachel
who: A Buzite of the family of Ram and the father of Elihu, Job's young counselor.
key: He is named as the father of Elihu, of the family of Ram (Job 32).
His son Elihu spoke in anger after Job's three friends fell silent (Job 32).

name: Barak
who: The son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali who led Israel's army against Sisera at Deborah's summons.
key: Deborah summoned him to lead ten thousand men, and he insisted she go with him (Judges 4).
He routed Sisera's army at Mount Tabor, though the honor of killing Sisera went to Jael (Judges 4).

name: Bariah
who: A descendant of David's royal line after the exile, one of the sons of Shemaiah.
key: The sons of Shemaiah were Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six (1 Chronicles 3).
Shemaiah was the son of Shecaniah, in the royal line of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3).

name: Barnabas
who: A Levite from Cyprus, called son of encouragement, who traveled with Paul as a missionary.
key: Joseph, called Barnabas by the apostles, sold a field and gave the money (Acts 4).
He brought the newly converted Saul to the apostles in Jerusalem (Acts 9).

name: Bartimaeus
who: A blind beggar near Jericho, son of Timaeus, whom Jesus healed on his way to Jerusalem.
key: Sitting by the road at Jericho, he cried out to Jesus, Son of David, for mercy (Mark 10).
Many rebuked him, but he cried out all the more, and Jesus called him (Mark 10).

name: Baruch
who: Son of Neriah, the scribe and faithful companion of the prophet Jeremiah.
key: Baruch received the deed of the field Jeremiah bought at Anathoth (Jeremiah 32).
He wrote Jeremiah's words on a scroll and read them in the temple (Jeremiah 36).

name: Barzillai
who: A wealthy elderly Gileadite of Rogelim who supplied David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: He brought beds, food, and supplies to David and his people at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 17).
At eighty years old he declined David's invitation to live in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 19).

name: Basemath
who: A wife of Esau, daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth, and mother of Reuel.
key: To please Isaac, Esau married a daughter of Ishmael, sister of Nebaioth (Genesis 28).
She is named as Esau's wife, Ishmael's daughter (Genesis 36).

name: Bathsheba
who: The wife of Uriah whom David took in adultery; she later married David and became Solomon's mother.
key: David saw her bathing, slept with her, and arranged Uriah's death in battle (2 Samuel 11).
Their first child died, and she later bore Solomon, whom the Lord loved (2 Samuel 12).

name: Bebai
who: The father, or family head, of Zechariah, who led twenty-eight men back from Babylon with Ezra.
key: Zechariah son of Bebai returned from Babylon to Jerusalem in Ezra's company (Ezra 8).
Twenty-eight men of the family of Bebai were registered with him (Ezra 8).

name: Bedad
who: Father of Hadad, a king of Edom who defeated Midian in the country of Moab.
key: After Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad reigned in Edom (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats Hadad son of Bedad among Edom's kings (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Beerah
who: A Reubenite chief, son of Baal, carried into exile by Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria.
key: Beerah son of Baal is named in the line of Joel in the tribe of Reuben (1 Chronicles 5).
He was a chief of the Reubenites (1 Chronicles 5).

name: Bela
who: Son of Beor and the first king listed as reigning in Edom, before any king reigned over Israel.
key: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites (Genesis 36).
The name of his city was Dinhabah (Genesis 36).

name: Bela
who: The firstborn son of Benjamin and head of the Belaite clan.
key: He is listed among the sons of Benjamin who went to Egypt with Jacob (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Belaites in the tribe of Benjamin (Numbers 26).

name: Belshazzar
who: King of Babylon who misused the temple vessels and was killed the night the handwriting appeared.
key: Daniel received a vision of four beasts in Belshazzar's first year (Daniel 7).
Daniel saw the vision of the ram and goat in Belshazzar's third year (Daniel 8).

name: Ben-ammi
who: The son of Lot by his younger daughter and the ancestor of the Ammonites.
key: After Sodom's destruction, Lot's younger daughter conceived by her father in a cave near Zoar (Genesis 19).
She bore a son, named him Ben-ammi, and he became the father of the Ammonites (Genesis 19).

name: Ben-hadad
who: King of Syria in Damascus, son of Tabrimmon, who attacked Israel at the request of King Asa.
key: Asa of Judah sent him silver and gold to break his treaty with Baasha (1 Kings 15).
He attacked Israelite cities including Ijon, Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah (1 Kings 15).

name: Ben-hadad
who: A king of Syria in Elisha's day who besieged Samaria and was later murdered by Hazael.
key: He mustered his army and besieged Samaria, causing a terrible famine in the city (2 Kings 6).
Falling sick, he sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover (2 Kings 8).

name: Ben-hadad
who: A king of Syria, son of Hazael, who oppressed Israel until King Jehoash defeated him.
key: The LORD gave Israel into the hands of Hazael and his son Ben-hadad (2 Kings 13).
He became king after Hazael died (2 Kings 13).

name: Benaiah
who: Son of Jehoiada, a mighty warrior of David who became commander of Solomon's army.
key: Benaiah commanded David's bodyguard, the Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Samuel 8).
He killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day (2 Samuel 23).

name: Benaiah
who: A warrior from Pirathon in Ephraim, one of David's mighty men and a division commander.
key: Benaiah of Pirathon is listed among David's Thirty, his elite warriors (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles includes him among David's mighty men as well (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Benaiah
who: A Levite musician appointed when David brought the ark of God to Jerusalem.
key: He was appointed among the Levite musicians to play harps (1 Chronicles 15).
He served in the music as the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15).

name: Benaiah
who: The father of Jehoiada, who became one of David's counselors after Ahithophel.
key: His son Jehoiada succeeded Ahithophel as one of David's counselors (1 Chronicles 27).
He is likely Benaiah son of Jehoiada, commander of David's bodyguard, listed earlier (1 Chronicles 27).

name: Benaiah
who: The father of Pelatiah, a leader of Jerusalem who died while Ezekiel prophesied.
key: In a vision Ezekiel saw Pelatiah son of Benaiah among twenty-five men at the temple's east gate (Ezekiel 11).
As Ezekiel prophesied against them, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died (Ezekiel 11).

name: Benjamin
who: A descendant of Jacob's son Benjamin, son of Bilhan, listed in his tribe's genealogy.
key: He is listed among the sons of Bilhan in the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7).
Bilhan's descendants included 17,200 mighty warriors ready for war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Benjamin
who: A man of Jerusalem who helped rebuild the city wall under Nehemiah.
key: He and Hasshub repaired the section of wall opposite their house (Nehemiah 3).
His work was part of the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls led by Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3).

name: Benjamin
who: One of the leaders who joined the procession at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall.
key: He went with the leaders of Judah behind the first thanksgiving choir on the wall (Nehemiah 12).
The people rejoiced at the dedication, and the joy was heard far away (Nehemiah 12).

name: Benjamin
who: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, ancestor of the tribe of Benjamin.
key: Rachel died giving birth to him; she named him Ben-oni, but Jacob called him Benjamin (Genesis 35).
Jacob kept him home when his brothers first went to Egypt for grain (Genesis 42).

name: Beor
who: Father of Bela, the first king listed as reigning in Edom before Israel had kings.
key: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah (Genesis 36).
Chronicles begins its list of Edom's kings with Bela son of Beor (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Beor
who: Father of Balaam, the diviner hired by Balak king of Moab to curse Israel.
key: Balak sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel (Numbers 22).
Balaam the son of Beor blessed Israel instead of cursing them (Numbers 24).

name: Berechiah
who: The son of Iddo and father of the post-exilic prophet Zechariah.
key: The word of the LORD came to his son Zechariah in Darius's second year (Zechariah 1).
Ezra calls Zechariah the son of Iddo, naming his grandfather (Ezra 5).

name: Beriah
who: A son of Asher and ancestor of the Beriite clan.
key: He went down to Egypt with Jacob's family (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Beriites (Numbers 26).

name: Beriah
who: A son of Ephraim, born after two of Ephraim's sons were killed by the men of Gath.
key: Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead were killed raiding Gath's livestock, and Ephraim mourned many days (1 Chronicles 7).
Ephraim's wife then bore a son, named Beriah because disaster had come on the house (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Beriah
who: A Benjaminite family head in Aijalon who, with Shema, drove out the inhabitants of Gath.
key: Beriah and Shema were heads of fathers' houses of the inhabitants of Aijalon (1 Chronicles 8).
They put to flight the inhabitants of Gath (1 Chronicles 8).

name: Bernice
who: A royal woman who accompanied King Agrippa when he heard Paul's defense in Caesarea.
key: She arrived with Agrippa at Caesarea to greet the new governor Festus (Acts 25).
She entered the audience hall with Agrippa amid great pomp to hear Paul (Acts 25).

name: Bethuel
who: Son of Nahor and Milcah, nephew of Abraham, and father of Rebekah and Laban.
key: He was born to Nahor and Milcah and became the father of Rebekah (Genesis 22).
With Laban, he agreed that Rebekah's marriage to Isaac came from the LORD (Genesis 24).

name: Bezalel
who: Craftsman of Judah, son of Uri, whom God filled with his Spirit to build the tabernacle.
key: God called Bezalel by name and filled him with skill for all craftsmanship (Exodus 31).
Moses announced his calling and said God had given him ability to teach (Exodus 35).

name: Bichri
who: Benjaminite, father of Sheba, who led a revolt against King David.
key: His son Sheba blew a trumpet and called Israel to abandon David (2 Samuel 20).
The head of Sheba the son of Bichri was thrown to Joab from Abel's wall (2 Samuel 20).

name: Bildad
who: Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's three friends who came to comfort him.
key: He came with Eliphaz and Zophar to comfort Job (Job 2).
He insisted God does not pervert justice and urged Job to seek him (Job 8).

name: Bilhah
who: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, who bore him Dan and Naphtali.
key: Laban gave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her servant (Genesis 29).
Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob, and she bore Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30).

name: Bilhan
who: A Horite of Seir, son of the chief Ezer, listed among Edom's early inhabitants.
key: He is listed among the sons of Ezer, a Horite chief in the land of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Bilhan
who: A Benjaminite, son of Jediael, whose sons headed fathers' houses of mighty warriors.
key: Bilhan is listed as the son of Jediael in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 7).
His sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Bimhal
who: A man of the tribe of Asher, son of Japhlet, named in Asher's genealogy.
key: Bimhal is named with Pasach and Ashvath as the sons of Japhlet (1 Chronicles 7).
Asher's descendants were heads of fathers' houses and mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Boaz
who: A worthy man of Bethlehem who redeemed and married Ruth, becoming David's great-grandfather.
key: Boaz, a relative of Elimelech, showed kindness to Ruth in his field (Ruth 2).
At the threshing floor, he promised to act as her redeemer (Ruth 3).

name: Bukki
who: A priest descended from Aaron through Eleazar, listed in the high-priestly line and among Ezra's ancestors.
key: Bukki son of Abishua is named in the line of Eleazar son of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6).
He was the father of Uzzi in this priestly line (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Bunah
who: A son of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Jerahmeel with Ram, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah (1 Chronicles 2).
His father Jerahmeel was the firstborn son of Hezron, grandson of Judah (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Buzi
who: The father of Ezekiel, the priest whom God called as a prophet among the exiles in Babylonia.
key: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, by the Chebar canal (Ezekiel 1).
Buzi is named only as the father of Ezekiel, who was among the exiles in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1).

name: Caiaphas
who: High priest during Jesus' ministry, son-in-law of Annas, who led the council's case against Jesus.
key: He was high priest, alongside Annas, when John the Baptist began preaching (Luke 3).
He said it was better for one man to die for the people, which John calls prophecy (John 11).

name: Cain
who: Firstborn son of Adam and Eve, who murdered his brother Abel.
key: A farmer, he brought an offering the LORD did not regard with favor (Genesis 4).
He killed his brother Abel in the field (Genesis 4).

name: Kenan
who: A son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel in the line from Adam to Noah.
key: He was born when his father Enosh was ninety years old (Genesis 5).
He fathered Mahalalel at seventy and lived 910 years (Genesis 5).

name: Cainan
who: A son of Arphaxad and father of Shelah, named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus.
key: Luke lists him between Arphaxad and Shelah in the ancestry of Jesus (Luke 3).
Genesis names Shelah directly as Arphaxad's son, without listing Cainan (Genesis 11).

name: Caleb
who: Son of Jephunneh from Judah, one of the twelve spies, who wholly followed the Lord.
key: As one of twelve spies, Caleb urged Israel to go up and take the land (Numbers 13).
God promised that Caleb and Joshua alone of their generation would enter Canaan (Numbers 14).

name: Caleb
who: A son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah, whose wives and many descendants are listed in Chronicles.
key: He is named, as Chelubai, among the sons of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).
He fathered children by Azubah and later married Ephrath, who bore Hur (1 Chronicles 2).

name: Canaan
who: Son of Ham and grandson of Noah, ancestor of the Canaanite peoples whose land bore his name.
key: Noah cursed Canaan after Ham saw his father's nakedness (Genesis 9).
His descendants included Sidon, Heth, the Jebusites, the Amorites, and other peoples (Genesis 10).

name: Carmi
who: A man of Judah, son of Zabdi, whose son Achan brought trouble on Israel at Jericho.
key: He is named as son of Zabdi, of the clan of Zerah in Judah (Joshua 7).
His son Achan took devoted things from Jericho and was found out by lot (Joshua 7).

name: Calcol
who: A famous wise man, a son of Mahol, whose wisdom Solomon surpassed.
key: Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4).
Solomon's fame spread to all the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4).

name: Chedorlaomer
who: A king of Elam who led an alliance of kings in the days of Abram.
key: Several kings served him twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth (Genesis 14).
He and his allies defeated the kings of the valley and captured Lot (Genesis 14).

name: Chemosh
label: False god
who: The national god of Moab, for whom King Solomon built a high place east of Jerusalem.
key: An ancient song declared Moab undone, calling its people the people of Chemosh (Numbers 21).
Jephthah told the Ammonite king to keep what his god Chemosh had given him (Judges 11).

name: Chenaanah
who: The father of Zedekiah, a false prophet in King Ahab's court.
key: His son Zedekiah made iron horns and promised Ahab victory over Syria (1 Kings 22).
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah struck the prophet Micaiah on the cheek (2 Chronicles 18).

name: Chenaanah
who: A Benjaminite, son of Bilhan, whose family was counted among Benjamin's mighty warriors.
key: The sons of Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7).
They were heads of fathers' houses, mighty warriors, 17,200 able to go to war (1 Chronicles 7).

name: Cheran
who: A Horite, son of Dishon, among the clans of Seir who lived in the land before Esau's descendants.
key: The sons of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats these sons of Dishon among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Chimham
who: A man who went to Jerusalem with King David in place of the aged Barzillai.
key: Barzillai asked David to take his servant Chimham in his place (2 Samuel 19).
David promised to do for Chimham whatever Barzillai wished, and Chimham went on with the king (2 Samuel 19).

name: Claudius
who: The Roman emperor during part of the early church's spread, mentioned twice in Acts.
key: Agabus foretold a great famine, which took place in the days of Claudius (Acts 11).
Claudius commanded all the Jews to leave Rome, so Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth (Acts 18).

name: Col-hozeh
who: Father of Shallun, who ruled the district of Mizpah and rebuilt the Fountain Gate under Nehemiah.
key: Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Col-hozeh's son also built the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the king's garden (Nehemiah 3).

name: Cornelius
who: A God-fearing Roman centurion at Caesarea whose household received the Holy Spirit through Peter's preaching.
key: A devout centurion who prayed and gave alms, he saw an angel in a vision (Acts 10).
At the angel's word he sent men to Joppa to bring Simon Peter (Acts 10).

name: Cozbi
who: A Midianite woman, daughter of the chief Zur, killed with Zimri by Phinehas at Peor.
key: Zimri brought her into the camp in the sight of Moses while Israel wept (Numbers 25).
Phinehas pierced them both with a spear, and the plague on Israel stopped (Numbers 25).

name: Cush
who: A son of Ham and grandson of Noah, the father of Nimrod; his name later designates a land south of Egypt.
key: He is listed as the first son of Ham in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
His sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca (Genesis 10).

name: The Cushite
who: The runner Joab sent to report Absalom's death to King David.
key: Joab sent him to tell David what he had seen (2 Samuel 18).
Ahimaaz ran after him and outran him (2 Samuel 18).

name: Cushi
who: The father of the prophet Zephaniah and a descendant of Hezekiah through Gedaliah and Amariah.
key: The word of the LORD came to Zephaniah son of Cushi in the days of King Josiah (Zephaniah 1).
Cushi's ancestry is traced through Gedaliah and Amariah back to Hezekiah (Zephaniah 1).

name: Cyrus
who: King of Persia who allowed the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.
key: Isaiah named him as the LORD's shepherd who would order Jerusalem rebuilt (Isaiah 44).
The LORD called him his anointed, whose right hand he had grasped (Isaiah 45).

name: Dagon
label: False god
who: A god of the Philistines, whose image fell broken before the ark of the LORD in Ashdod.
key: The Philistine lords gathered to sacrifice to Dagon, crediting him with Samson's capture (Judges 16).
Samson pulled down the house of Dagon, dying with the Philistines inside (Judges 16).

name: Damaris
who: A woman in Athens who believed after hearing Paul's address at the Areopagus.
key: Paul addressed the Areopagus in Athens, proclaiming the Creator who raised Jesus from the dead (Acts 17).
Some mocked, but some men joined Paul and believed (Acts 17).

name: Dan
who: Son of Jacob by Rachel's servant Bilhah, ancestor of the tribe of Dan.
key: Rachel named him Dan, saying God had judged her and given her a son (Genesis 30).
Jacob blessed him, saying Dan would judge his people (Genesis 49).

name: Daniel
who: Young Judean taken to Babylon who served faithfully in royal courts and received visions from God.
key: Taken to Babylon, he refused the king's food and was renamed Belteshazzar (Daniel 1).
God revealed to him Nebuchadnezzar's dream and its meaning (Daniel 2).

name: Darda
who: A famous wise man, a son of Mahol, whose wisdom Solomon surpassed.
key: Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol (1 Kings 4).
Solomon's fame spread to all the surrounding nations (1 Kings 4).

name: Darius
who: King of Persia during whose reign the second temple in Jerusalem was rebuilt and completed.
key: Work on the temple stopped until the second year of his reign (Ezra 4).
Haggai prophesied in his second year, urging the people to rebuild (Haggai 1).

name: Darius the Mede
who: Median ruler who received Babylon's kingdom and was forced by his own decree to cast Daniel to lions.
key: At about sixty-two years old he received the kingdom after Belshazzar's death (Daniel 5).
He set 120 satraps over the kingdom, with Daniel among three officials over them (Daniel 6).

name: Dathan
who: Reubenite son of Eliab who, with his brother Abiram, joined Korah's rebellion against Moses.
key: With Abiram and Korah, he rose up against the leadership of Moses and Aaron (Numbers 16).
He and Abiram refused Moses' summons, accusing him of failing to bring them to the promised land (Numbers 16).

name: Lot's younger daughter
who: The younger daughter of Lot, who fled Sodom with him and became the mother of Ben-ammi.
key: Angels led her, her sister, and her parents out of Sodom before its destruction (Genesis 19).
She and her sister lived with Lot in a cave in the hills near Zoar (Genesis 19).

name: Pharaoh's daughter
who: The Egyptian princess who found the infant Moses in the Nile and raised him as her son.
key: She found the baby Moses in a basket among the reeds and took pity on him (Exodus 2).
At Miriam's suggestion, she paid Moses' own mother to nurse him (Exodus 2).

name: Daughter of Pharaoh
who: The Egyptian princess whom Solomon married.
key: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh and brought her into the city of David (1 Kings 3).
Solomon built her a house like his Hall of Judgment (1 Kings 7).

name: David
who: Shepherd from Bethlehem who became Israel's greatest king, a psalmist, and ancestor of the Messiah.
key: Samuel anointed the young shepherd David as the next king of Israel (1 Samuel 16).
He killed the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17).

name: Debir
who: The Amorite king of Eglon who joined a coalition against Gibeon and was defeated by Joshua.
key: Adoni-zedek of Jerusalem called him to join in attacking Gibeon for making peace with Israel (Joshua 10).
After the battle he and four other kings hid in a cave at Makkedah (Joshua 10).

name: Deborah
who: Prophetess and judge of Israel who summoned Barak to defeat Sisera's Canaanite army.
key: As a prophetess and wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel under a palm tree (Judges 4).
She summoned Barak and relayed God's command to fight Sisera at Mount Tabor (Judges 4).

name: Dedan
who: A son of Raamah and great-grandson of Ham, listed in the Table of Nations after the flood.
key: Dedan is listed with his brother Sheba as a son of Raamah, son of Cush (Genesis 10).
Chronicles repeats him among Raamah's sons in the line of Ham (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Dedan
who: A grandson of Abraham and Keturah, son of Jokshan, whose descendants included the Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
key: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan (Genesis 25).
The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim (Genesis 25).

name: Delaiah
who: Son of Mehetabel and father of Shemaiah, who tried to frighten Nehemiah into hiding in the temple.
key: Nehemiah went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel (Nehemiah 6).
Delaiah's son urged Nehemiah to hide in the temple, but Nehemiah saw he had been hired (Nehemiah 6).

name: Delilah
who: A woman of the Valley of Sorek whom Samson loved and who betrayed him to the Philistines.
key: Samson loved Delilah, who lived in the Valley of Sorek (Judges 16).
Philistine lords each offered her silver to learn the secret of his strength (Judges 16).

name: Demas
who: A coworker of Paul who later deserted him for love of the present world.
key: He sent greetings to the Colossians along with Luke (Colossians 4).
Paul named him among his fellow workers when writing to Philemon (Philemon 1).

name: Demetrius
who: A silversmith of Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and stirred up a riot against Paul.
key: His trade brought much business to the craftsmen of Ephesus (Acts 19).
He warned them Paul's preaching endangered their trade and Artemis's temple, and the city filled with confusion (Acts 19).

name: Diblaim
who: The father of Gomer, the wife whom the prophet Hosea married at the LORD's command.
key: Hosea took Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, as his wife at the LORD's command (Hosea 1).
Diblaim's daughter bore Hosea a son named Jezreel, then Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi (Hosea 1).

name: Dinah
who: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, whose violation by Shechem led her brothers to take violent revenge.
key: Leah bore her to Jacob after six sons (Genesis 30).
Shechem, son of Hamor, seized and violated her, then sought to marry her (Genesis 34).

name: Dionysius
who: A member of the Areopagus council in Athens who believed after hearing Paul.
key: He heard Paul proclaim the resurrection before the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17).
He joined Paul and believed, along with a woman named Damaris and others (Acts 17).

name: Diotrephes
who: A church leader who loved to be first and refused to welcome John's messengers.
key: John says he likes to put himself first and does not acknowledge John's authority (3 John 1).
He spoke wicked nonsense, refused traveling brothers, and expelled those who welcomed them (3 John 1).

name: Dishan
who: A son of Seir the Horite and a Horite chief in Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Seir, inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons Uz and Aran are named, and he was a Horite chief (Genesis 36).

name: Dishon
who: A son of Seir the Horite and a chief among the Horites who lived in Seir before Esau's descendants.
key: Dishon was one of the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).

name: Dodanim
who: A son of Javan and descendant of Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations among the coastland peoples.
key: He is listed among the sons of Javan, son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
Chronicles gives the name as Rodanim in the same list (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Dodo
who: A man of Issachar, father of Puah and grandfather of Tola, who judged Israel after Abimelech.
key: Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel (Judges 10).
Tola judged Israel twenty-three years and was buried at Shamir (Judges 10).

name: Dodo
who: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, one of the three chief warriors among David's mighty men.
key: His son Eleazar was one of the three mighty men who were with David (2 Samuel 23).
Eleazar son of Dodo stood with David against the Philistines at Pas-dammim (1 Chronicles 11).

name: Doeg
who: An Edomite, chief of Saul's herdsmen, who betrayed Ahimelech and killed the priests of Nob.
key: He was at Nob, detained before the LORD, when David received bread and Goliath's sword (1 Samuel 21).
He told Saul he had seen Ahimelech help David (1 Samuel 22).

name: Tabitha
who: A disciple in Joppa known for good works and charity, whom Peter raised from the dead.
key: She was full of good works and acts of charity among the believers in Joppa (Acts 9).
She fell sick and died, and the disciples sent to Lydda for Peter (Acts 9).

name: Drusilla
who: The Jewish wife of the Roman governor Felix, who heard Paul speak in Caesarea.
key: She came with Felix, who sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus (Acts 24).
As Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and judgment, Felix grew alarmed and sent him away (Acts 24).

name: Ebal
who: A Horite of Seir, son of Shobal, listed among the early inhabitants of Edom.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shobal, son of Seir the Horite (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats him among the descendants of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

name: Ebed-melech
who: An Ethiopian eunuch in King Zedekiah's palace who rescued Jeremiah from a muddy cistern.
key: He appealed to King Zedekiah on behalf of Jeremiah, left to die in a cistern (Jeremiah 38).
With thirty men and old rags, he drew Jeremiah up out of the cistern (Jeremiah 38).

name: Ebed
who: The father of Gaal, who led the men of Shechem against Abimelech.
key: His son Gaal moved into Shechem, and its leaders put confidence in him (Judges 9).
Gaal challenged Abimelech but was defeated and driven out of Shechem (Judges 9).

name: Eber
who: A descendant of Shem through Shelah, father of Peleg and Joktan, and an ancestor of Abraham.
key: He is named in the table of nations, where Shem is called the father of all Eber's children (Genesis 10).
He fathered Peleg at thirty-four and lived many years afterward (Genesis 11).

name: Ebiasaph
who: A Levite descended from Kohath through Korah, ancestor of singers and gatekeepers.
key: He is listed among the sons of Korah (Exodus 6).
He appears in the Kohathite line leading to Heman the singer (1 Chronicles 6).

name: Eder
who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mushi, listed in David's Levite divisions.
key: He is listed among the sons of Mushi when David organized the Levites (1 Chronicles 23).
He is named again when the Levites cast lots for duties as the priests did (1 Chronicles 24).

name: Eglon
who: A king of Moab who oppressed Israel for eighteen years until Ehud killed him.
key: Because Israel did evil, the LORD strengthened Eglon, who with Ammon and Amalek took the city of palms (Judges 3).
Israel served him eighteen years (Judges 3).

name: Ehud
who: Left-handed Benjaminite judge who killed Eglon king of Moab and delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.
key: After Israel served Eglon eighteen years, the LORD raised up Ehud as a deliverer (Judges 3).
He brought Israel's tribute to Eglon and killed him with a hidden double-edged sword (Judges 3).
